text: We always joked about AI agents are infinite interns.  In fact, interns are still light years ahead of LLM/AI.   I have to babysit an AI 15 minutes to get something done and often ends up in frustration, I only have to give a 15 second instruction to my intern to get the same thing done.. #AMDBrandAmbassador

author.name: Jakob Prince
author.headline: AI Strategy at PromptQL | Accurate AI for teams with Shared Context

comments.text:
I would argue that because while interns are often lacking in information and inexperience to always make the correct decision, at least they tell you when they're unsure and learn from instruction to better themselves. This contrasts from most unadaptive AI systems being "confidently wrong" and not learning like a human.

This is what we've tried to address with PromptQL. Creating an AI system that signals its confidence levels, surfaces ambiguity in its responses, learns from feedback, and improves its knowledge of a company's terminology, processes, and tribal knowledge (just like an intern... one that never sleeps that is)
